title: Exercise 7C · Q4
summary: Use the formulas for the foot of a perpendicular in a right-angled triangle to confirm X is that point.
alt: Exercise 7C · Q4: A rectangular grass patch, PQRS, has sides 40 m and 30 m. A straight path which cuts through the grass patch joins S and Q. Lamppost X is located on SQ such that SX : XQ = 16 : 9 and RX = 24 m. Jun Wei walks along the path and stops at a point which is nearest to R. Show that he stops at X.

hyp.label: Hypotenuse
hyp.text: The side opposite the right angle. It is always the longest side.

legA.label: Shorter side 1
legA.text: One of the two sides that meet at the right angle.

legB.label: Shorter side 2
legB.text: The other side that meets at the right angle.

steps.title: The question
steps.narration: A rectangular grass patch **PQRS** has sides **40 m** and **30 m**. A path joins **S** and **Q**. Lamppost **X** lies on **SQ** such that **SX : XQ = 16 : 9**, and **RX = 24 m**. Show that **X** is the point on **SQ** nearest to **R**.

steps.title: Right angle and theorem
steps.narration: In ΔSRQ, **∠R = 90°**, so the **hypotenuse** is the side opposite it: **SQ**. The other two sides meet at the right angle. **Pythagoras' theorem**: the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{SQ^2} &= \role{legA}{SR^2} + \role{legB}{RQ^2}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Substitute and add
steps.narration: Put in the lengths, square them and add.\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{SQ^2} &= \role{legA}{SR^2} + \role{legB}{RQ^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{40^2} + \role{legB}{30^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{1600} + \role{legB}{900} \\ &= \role{hyp}{2500}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Square root
steps.narration: Take the square root of both sides (a length is positive).\[\begin{aligned}\role{hyp}{SQ^2} &= \role{legA}{SR^2} + \role{legB}{RQ^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{40^2} + \role{legB}{30^2} \\ &= \role{legA}{1600} + \role{legB}{900} \\ &= \role{hyp}{2500} \\ \role{hyp}{SQ} &= \sqrt{2500} = \role{ans}{50\ \text{m}}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Split SQ in the ratio 16:9
steps.narration: **SX : XQ = 16 : 9**, so **SQ** splits into **25** equal parts.\[\begin{aligned}SX &= 50\times\tfrac{16}{25} = 32\ \text{m} \\ XQ &= 50\times\tfrac{9}{25} = 18\ \text{m}\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: The foot of the perpendicular from R
steps.narration: For a right-angled **ΔSRQ**, the foot of the perpendicular from **R** to **SQ** splits **SQ** into **SR²/SQ** and **RQ²/SQ**, and that perpendicular has length **(SR × RQ)/SQ**.\[\begin{aligned}\frac{SR^2}{SQ} &= \frac{40^2}{50} = 32\ \text{m}\quad(\text{matches } SX) \\ \frac{RQ^2}{SQ} &= \frac{30^2}{50} = 18\ \text{m}\quad(\text{matches } XQ) \\ \frac{SR\times RQ}{SQ} &= \frac{40\times 30}{50} = \role{ans}{24\ \text{m}}\quad(\text{matches } RX)\end{aligned}\]

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.narration: Every check matches: **X** divides **SQ** exactly where the foot of the perpendicular from **R** would fall, **and** **RX = 24 m** is exactly that perpendicular length. So **X is the point on SQ nearest to R**, and Jun Wei stops at **X**.

formulas.title: Pythagoras' theorem
formulas.text: In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides.

formulas.title: Finding the hypotenuse
formulas.text: Add the two squares, then take the square root.

formulas.title: Finding a shorter side
formulas.text: Subtract the known shorter side's square from the hypotenuse's square, then take the square root.

challenges.title: Check SQ
challenges.prompt: SR = 40 m and RQ = 30 m, right angle at R. Find SQ.

takeaways: In a right-angled triangle, the foot of the perpendicular from the right-angle vertex to the hypotenuse divides it into **leg²/hyp** pieces.
The perpendicular's own length is **(leg × leg) / hyp**.
Keep a few extra decimal places in the middle of a calculation and round only the **final** answer (3 s.f.).

notes.title: Exam tip
notes.text: Always begin with a line such as "In ΔABC, ∠C = 90°. Using Pythagoras' Theorem," — it shows which triangle and which right angle you are using.
